body: QUESTIONABLE. 032 lead amplitudes, not recomputed: 0.152868766846 mm and 0.0652229064039 mm at 60 psi, and 0.089173447327 mm and 0.0380466954023 mm at 35 psi. Zero-to-peak wrinkle components. Cell scale: NASA ER-1001, NTRS 19950020773, Figure 25, dimple depth 0.000065 inch, 0.001651 mm, on 3/16-inch foil coupons. That is 0.0434 of the smallest and exceeds none. The 3/8-inch cells are slopes of 0.5 to 1.6 milliradian, not a depth. A one-cell rise at the larger slope is a projection, 0.01524 mm, still under. Short wave: Woody, Proc. IEEE 82, May 1994, epoxies 1 mm aluminum onto a machined honeycomb core. Measured scales are greater than 40 mm. Under 10 mm is a 2 micrometre sheet finish, averaged over 10 mm, so the cell is not separate. Installed estimate 24 micrometres rms sits under the smallest amplitude and is not that component. Whole panel: von Hoerner, NRAO report 30, 1969, quotes honeycomb at 0.008 inch, 0.2032 mm, printed as 0.20 mm rms. That number is larger than every needed amplitude and is a vendor panel rms, not a cell depth. Per-foot shop bows on the 032 card are the same mismatch. AMS7902G section 1.3 names three flatness classes. Section 3.5.5 was not in the three pages obtained. Revision H was not opened. No class number is stated. No beryllium-face amplitude at the wrinkle wavelength was obtained. Elapsed 0.000121840741485 s. Not a certification. The caps-open order stays open.
